summary: I checked every stated result and proof on the page: Legendre symbol and Euler's criterion (the counting argument, multiplicativity via congruence mod p, and the a=-1 case are all correct), the splitting theorem for Q(sqrt(d)) including the p=2 cases (Kummer–Dedekind is applicable with index 1, and the mod-2 factorizations x^2, (x+1)^2, x(x-1), x^2+x+1 are computed correctly), the Gauss sum computation g^2=p* (the substitution b=ac, the inner sums -1 and p-1, and the final chain g^2=(-1/p)p - sum(c/p) all check out), the uniqueness of the quadratic subfield, the Frobenius restriction lemma (the unramifiedness of q in F is correctly derived, and uniqueness of Frobenius is applied legitimately), the reciprocity proof (Steps 2-4 correctly combine Gauss-sum item 2, the splitting theorem for F=Q(sqrt(p*)) with q∤p*, and the first supplementary law), the second supplementary law via Q(zeta_8) (sqrt(2)=zeta+zeta^{-1}, the sign behaviour of sigma_p, and the parity check of (p^2-1)/8 are all correct), the two-squares example, the Kronecker-Weber remark, the hypcheck bullets and both problem solutions ((3/p)=1 iff p≡±1 mod 12, and (5/p)=(p/5), 5=5*=(zeta-zeta^2-zeta^3+zeta^4)^2). I found no false statement, no unjustified inference beyond routine one-line checks, and no circularity.
